issues.legal_issue: A beneficiary may waive mandatory safeguards governing a secured-property sale, and a written consent accepted by the creditor may establish an agreed extension for payment of the sale balance.
material_facts: The secured property was auctioned before the required notice interval had elapsed, and the borrower was present but did not object to the timing.
The purchaser’s payment of the initial deposit was disputed as not having been made in the required manner, and the purchaser did not pay the balance within the ordinary payment period.
The borrower later wrote to the creditor consenting to acceptance of the remaining sale price and issuance of a sale certificate to the purchaser; the creditor accepted that consent.
The purchaser paid the balance on the day the borrower gave that written consent, and the creditor issued the sale certificate.
issues.conclusion: The relevant mandatory requirements were made for the benefit of the borrower or secured creditor and could be waived by them. The borrower waived the relevant safeguards through his conduct and written consent; the accepted letter, together with the purchaser’s payment, substantially satisfied the requirement for a written agreement extending the payment period. The sale certificate should not have been quashed on these grounds.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 9(1) and Rule 9(3) of the Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules, 2002 are mandatory, while the payment period in Rule 9(4) may be extended by a written agreement between the parties. A mandatory provision made for the benefit of a party may be waived by that party unless the provision indicates otherwise. A written agreement under Rule 9(4) requires no prescribed form and means a written manifestation of mutual assent; the parties for this purpose are the secured creditor, borrower, and purchaser.

rule.if: secured_property_auction and (sale_before_notice_interval or disputed_initial_deposit or balance_paid_late) and borrower_present_without_objection and borrower_wrote_consent_to_late_payment_and_certificate and creditor_accepted_consent and purchaser_paid_balance_after_consent

predicates.secured_property_auction: A secured creditor arranged an auction sale of immovable property to enforce a security interest.
predicates.sale_before_notice_interval: The creditor conducted the auction before the required interval following publication or service of the sale notice had elapsed.
predicates.disputed_initial_deposit: A dispute arose over whether the purchaser made the required initial deposit in the required manner.
predicates.balance_paid_late: The purchaser paid the remaining sale price after the ordinary payment period had expired.
predicates.borrower_present_without_objection: The borrower attended the auction and did not object to its timing.
predicates.borrower_wrote_consent_to_late_payment_a: The borrower sent the creditor written consent to accept the purchaser’s late balance payment and issue the sale certificate.
predicates.creditor_accepted_consent: The creditor accepted the borrower’s written consent.
predicates.purchaser_paid_balance_after_consent: The purchaser paid the remaining sale price after the borrower gave consent.

issues.definition: When a secured-property auction has procedural departures and the borrower, present at the auction, later gives written consent accepted by the creditor for the purchaser’s late payment and certificate, the departures are treated as waived or substantially satisfied once the purchaser pays the balance.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court should ordinarily decline extraordinary writ relief against secured-creditor enforcement when an effective statutory remedy has not been used and the borrower’s conduct provides no justification for bypassing that remedy.
material_facts: The borrower defaulted despite earlier demands and a statutory demand notice, and the secured property was auctioned after the notice period had passed.
The borrower attended the auction without objecting to its timing and later gave written consent to acceptance of the purchaser’s delayed balance payment and issuance of the sale certificate.
The borrower did not pursue the available appeal before the specialist tribunal and instead sought writ relief.
The borrower challenged the sale certificate more than four years after it was issued.
issues.conclusion: Although an alternative remedy is not an absolute bar to writ jurisdiction, the High Court had no justification on these facts for allowing the borrower to bypass the effective statutory remedy. The writ orders were set aside and the borrower’s petitions were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 226 of the Constitution, the rule requiring exhaustion of an alternative remedy is discretionary, not an absolute jurisdictional bar. However, where an effective remedy is available under Section 17 of the SARFAESI Act and the statute supplies a detailed grievance-redress mechanism, the High Court should ordinarily require that remedy to be used first. The Court relied on United Bank of India v. Satyawati Tondon, (2010) 8 SCC 110.

rule.if: writ_challenge_to_secured_creditor_enforcement and effective_statutory_remedy_available and not statutory_remedy_used and borrower_defaulted_despite_demands and borrower_conducted_no_timely_objection_or_consent and challenge_brought_after_substantial_delay

predicates.writ_challenge_to_secured_creditor_enfor: A borrower brought a writ challenge to a secured creditor’s enforcement action.
predicates.effective_statutory_remedy_available: The borrower had access to an effective statutory process for challenging the enforcement action.
predicates.statutory_remedy_used: The borrower pursued the available statutory process before seeking writ relief.
predicates.borrower_defaulted_despite_demands: The borrower failed to repay despite demands for payment.
predicates.borrower_conducted_no_timely_objection_o: The borrower did not object when the auction occurred and later consented to the purchaser’s delayed payment and receipt of a sale certificate.
predicates.challenge_brought_after_substantial_dela: The borrower waited a substantial time after the sale certificate was issued before challenging the sale.

issues.definition: When a borrower challenges secured-creditor enforcement by writ despite an effective unused statutory remedy, and has defaulted, failed to object in time or has consented to the sale arrangements, and delayed the challenge, extraordinary writ relief is denied.
